utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Okay, um, let's start. Is everyone on?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Diego's still on mute, I think.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, I'm here. I was on with facilities about the, uh, badge readers on three.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Fine. Quick one first, the offsite headcount form.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Is that the one Nadia sent round on Monday?

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Yes. Deadline is Thursday, I think.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: It's Wednesday noon. I checked the email again this morning.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Wednesday then. Please fill it in before-

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: I already did mine. It's just dietary stuff and the-

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Oh, dietary, that reminds me, the venue last year had that, um, the lentil thing, the stew, and it was honestly the best thing I ate all spring.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Diego-

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: No, I'm serious, I asked the caterer for the name and they just said it was a family recipe, and then I tried to make it at home and it came out like, like wallpaper paste.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Did you use the right lentils though?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: That's the thing, I don't know what the right ones are. Red, green, there's a brown one-

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Can we get the form sorted before the lentils?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, sorry. Tangent. Done.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Thanks. So, um. The main thing today is the first round for engineering hires.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Right, the whole, you know, how we open the funnel for them.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Yes. Priya, you had something on that?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: I do. Um, give me a sec, I've got the sheet open somewhere.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Is this the thing from the chat thread? Because Irina already said-

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Different thing. Irina was talking about scheduling.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Oh. Okay.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: So, right now every engineering candidate gets a phone screen first, twenty or thirty minutes with one of us. What if we dropped that and just sent them a short exercise instead? Thirty minutes, they do it on their own time, we review what comes back.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Like a take-home.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Yes, a take-home. Small, nothing huge.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Hm. Okay. I mean, I've done those as a candidate and they never stay thirty minutes.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: That's fair, and I'd cap it. Hard cap, the instructions say so.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: But why though? What's wrong with the phone screen? It's-

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: It's not that it's wrong, it's that it's uneven. Look, last quarter I pulled the pass rates by recruiter. One of them was passing about 38 percent of people to the next stage.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: And another one was at 61. Same kinds of candidates, same positions. A take-home gives everyone the identical task, so we're comparing like with like.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay, but 61 and 38, that could just be who they happened to get.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Could be. I don't think it explains the whole gap, though.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: I mean, directionally it feels right? Like, consistency matters.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Directionally, yes.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Who were the two? Without names, I mean.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: I'd rather not say in the meeting. It's in the sheet, I can share it.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Okay. Mm.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Is it the sample size? How many screens each, roughly?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Um, I think around forty for the low one and, hang on, thirty-something for the other. I'd have to check.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Thirty-something is not a lot.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: No, it isn't. That's why I'm saying directionally.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: And what about people who just won't do it? Because I'd skip it.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Yeah, senior people especially. They've got three other offers.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: That's a real risk. I don't have a number on that.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Maybe Kaveh would know. He's on the engineering side.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: He might. I could ask him how it went when they tried it for the data team.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Did they try that? I never heard.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Last year, I think. Or the year before. Daan mentioned it once.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: It was last year. Because it was around when we had the, uh, the audit.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Okay. Maybe. I'll ask.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: The other thing is who looks at the results. It's not us, right?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: No, someone technical would. Not us.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Then that's, you know, that's a cost for them. Their time.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Sure. Although they're already on the phone screens sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Not that often. Stefan did two last month and complained about it.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Right, which is its own cost.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Hm.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: What about candidates who aren't, like, English first language? A written exercise could be-

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: It's code, though. Mostly code.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Mostly. Sometimes there's a write-up.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: There wouldn't be a write-up in thirty minutes. It'd be a small problem and a short note, at most.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Okay, that's different then.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: I do wonder if it's, um, if it's too early. For the first thing they see from us.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Like it's asking something of them before we've given them anything. A call at least is a conversation.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: That's a fair point. The phone screen also sells the company a bit.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: It does. People tell me that.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Yeah. I don't have an answer for that one.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: And the screen does catch the obvious stuff, like people who aren't a fit on salary or location.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: We could ask those in the application form.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: We could. We don't right now.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: It's a field, though. Not hard.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Wait, what happens to the ones who fail the exercise, do they get feedback?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: I hadn't gotten that far.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Because that was the complaint with the other company's version, no one ever heard back.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: The, um, I forget. Someone mentioned it at the meetup.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Okay. We would have to answer people. That's right.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: How long would that take, per person?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: If it's a rubric, maybe ten minutes. Maybe more at the start.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Mm. And how many a month are we talking?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Last quarter we did, I want to say, a hundred and eighty screens. Roughly.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: So that's, what, thirty hours?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Thirty if everyone takes ten minutes. It won't be that neat.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: No. Right.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: That's more than the calls cost, probably.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Not sure. The calls are thirty minutes plus notes.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay, so about the same.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: About the same, but the quality of the comparison is better. That's my argument.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Okay. I want to think about it. Um, I'm not ready to say yes or no on this today.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Fair.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: I'm not either, honestly.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: I'd like to see the sheet first.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: I'll put it in the shared folder. And I'll ask Kaveh about the data team.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Good. Let's leave it there for today, then.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Can I ask one unrelated thing before we go? The agency invoice.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: The one from March?

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Yes, Anika said finance bounced it back. Wrong PO number or something.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: I'll take that. Send me the thread.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Will do.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Anything else? I have another call at the top of the hour.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: No. Thanks, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Okay, um. Everyone here? Good.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Here. Sorry, I was still finding the, uh, the link.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: It's the same link as last week, Diego.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Is it? Huh. I had a different one in my calendar.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Right. Before we get into the first-round thing, did anyone hear back from Anika about the March invoice?

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Yeah, she said finance re-sent it with the right PO. It should clear this month.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Good. That's one off the list.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Can I go back to last week for a second? I put the pass-rate sheet in the shared folder, and I think only Diego opened it.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: I did. I did open it. The, um, the tabs are a bit-

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: The tabs are labelled by quarter, it's not complicated.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: No, no, I'm just saying I got lost on the second one.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: That's the raw export. Ignore it.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: I read it. Well, the first page.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: That's fine. First page is the one that matters.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: So, um. Did anybody get anything on the data team?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: I emailed Kaveh Monday. Nothing yet.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Oh, I've got something on that. I ran into Kaveh in the kitchen on Tuesday-

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Wait, which kitchen?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Four. Anyway, he pulled it up for me. Their take-home last spring, they sent it to a hundred and twenty people, and forty-six of them just never sent it back. Gone.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: And the ones who did finish told them it ate around three hours. Not thirty minutes.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Forty-six out of a hundred and twenty. That's, what, close to forty percent?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: About that.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Three hours. Hm.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Was it capped, though? Did the instructions say stop at some point?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: He said it was supposed to be an hour, I think. People just kept going.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: That's what I said last week. They never stay the length you tell them.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Okay, so that's the number I didn't have. That's a real number.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: And I mean, it was the data team, so maybe engineers are different. But I doubt they're more patient.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: No, I'd assume it's worse. Senior people especially.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Can I - okay, so if the take-home loses that many people, what if we keep it a conversation, but make it, I don't know, properly structured? Forty-five minutes, on video, two of us on the call, same questions every time.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Two of us? On every screen?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Yeah, both scoring at the same time against one rubric. Like a shared sheet, each person fills in their own column.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: So not the same thing as the phone screen now.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: No, the phone screen is one person and their gut. This is two people and a sheet.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Which is basically my consistency point, just without the exercise.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Right, right, that's the idea. You get the same comparison you wanted, and nobody loses three hours of a Sunday.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: But the time, Diego. That's a lot of our time.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: It is. It's about ninety minutes of interviewer time per candidate, forty-five times two. Phone screen is thirty.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: So three times.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Roughly, yeah. But the take-home needed someone technical to read it anyway, so I'd say it's not free either.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: It'd be less than ninety, though. Ten minutes a review, I said.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Sure, but then you lose a hundred and twenty candidates, or whatever it was. Sorry, forty-six.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: I'm not saying no. I'm saying a hundred and eighty screens a quarter at ninety minutes is - that's a lot of hours.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Two hundred and seventy, if my math is right. Hang on.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Is that per month or the quarter?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Quarter. The hundred and eighty was the quarter.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Okay. So it's a lot but it's not a crazy lot.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: It's two hundred and seventy hours of people who have other jobs.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: I'd want to know whether the engineers would even agree to sit on those.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Stefan complained about two phone screens last month.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Stefan complains about everything.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Let's park that. We don't have to settle it today.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Agreed. I'd just like both options in the sheet next to each other.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Please. Can you do that?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Yes. I'll add a column for the video one with Diego's numbers.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: They're rough numbers, just so you know.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Oh, while we're here, can I raise a different thing? Onboarding. Laptops.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Go on.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: So right now the new starters come to the office on day one and pick up their laptop from IT. What if we just posted them out? Courier it to their home the Friday before they start.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: To their house? Is that allowed?

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: It's done in loads of places. Nadia said sales does it for remote people already.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: How do they set up the account if they don't have the laptop?

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: IT sends the credentials separately. Daan's team has done that for the remote ones.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: And if it gets lost?

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: It's insured, I think. I'd have to check.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: What's the actual problem with the pickup, though?

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Honestly, it eats half of day one. The Tuesday pickup is the only slot, and the last three people we hired were stuck in the queue for about seventy minutes each. On average.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Seventy minutes of their first morning, standing around.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Yeah. And then you've got a person sitting there and nothing to do on a laptop that isn't set up.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: That's actually fair. I waited for mine for like an hour on my first day, and I remember thinking, am I in the wrong building.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: You were in the wrong building.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: That was a different time. Different - yeah, okay.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: How much is the courier?

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Maybe fifteen, twenty pounds a box. I'll get an actual quote from Irina.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Fine. That's small.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: And who tracks that it arrived?

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: IT would. We just give them the start date.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Okay. Um. I'm fine with that. Ship the laptops to the new hires' homes the Friday before they start. Jonas, can you tell IT?

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: I'll message Daan today.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Does that start with the next hire?

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Next one, yes.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Ha, good. Okay, that was quick.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Faster than the interview thing.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: The interview thing has more moving parts.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: It does. Priya, the sheet, then we'll look again.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Will do. I'll have it before the next one.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: I have to jump, I've got a two o'clock.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Go. Thanks, all.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Okay, um. Everyone here? Good.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Here. Sorry, I was just-

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Can we do the interview thing first? I've got a hard stop at half past.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Yes. That's, um, that's what I wanted. We've been round it twice now.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Three times if you count the chat thread.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Nobody counts the chat thread.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: I'd like to be done with it today. Priya, you added the, the column?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: I did. Both of them side by side, same rows, so you can read straight across.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Take-home is about ten minutes a review, plus a reply to every single candidate. I put that in.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: And the drop-off? Kaveh's number?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Forty-six out of a hundred and twenty. It's highlighted in yellow.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: That's the one that gets me. You can't un-lose those people.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Mm. But that was the data team. Maybe engineers are, you know, different.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: I said that last week. I still don't think they're more patient.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: And I'd assume it's worse for seniors, like I said. They've got offers sitting there.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Can I say, the three hours thing? That was what stuck with me. Someone's Sunday, gone, for us.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: It wasn't for us, it was-

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: For the data team, I know, I know. Same idea though.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: So the take-home is, what, off the table then?

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: I didn't say that. I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: It's not dead for me. The consistency argument is still the best thing about it.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: But the video one has the consistency too. Two people, one rubric, it's-

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Same questions each time, yes. I know. That's why I kept it in the sheet.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: And no homework.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: And no homework. But it costs us more hours. I'm not hiding that.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: How many more? I forget what we landed on.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Ninety minutes of interviewer time against thirty. So roughly three times a phone screen.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Over a quarter that's, um, the hundred and eighty screens-

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Two seventy hours. Or around that. I redid it and I get about the same.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Two seventy hours of people who have day jobs.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Okay but not all of that is engineers. One of the two can be one of us.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Can it? Do we know enough to score a technical screen?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Not the coding bit, no. But the rubric has the other stuff. Communication, motivation, what they've shipped.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: That's actually in the draft rubric. Half the rows aren't technical.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Half?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Maybe a bit less than half. Five of eleven, something like that.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: So one of us, one engineer.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Right, that's what I had in my head.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: And they'd actually agree to that? Because Stefan-

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: I asked him, actually. I went to him directly.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: He said one a week is fine if it's on the calendar ahead of time. Two, he'd grumble. He didn't say no.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: That's a yes from Stefan.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: That's a grumbling yes.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: It's a number, anyway. One a week from him, and there's six or seven others on the list.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Do we know what they said?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Not all of them. I only asked Stefan and Kaveh.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Hm.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Sorry, can I go sideways for a sec? The offsite form. Nadia pinged me, she's still missing two.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Mine's in.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Mine's in. I think. I did it on the train.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Yours isn't. I looked at the sheet.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Huh. Okay. I'll do it after this.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: She needs it by Friday now, I think.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Wednesday was the old one. Friday is the extension.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Okay, Friday.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Speaking of the train, did anyone else get stuck on the Tuesday one? The whole line was down for, like, an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Diego-

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: No, because I ended up cycling in from the next station, which is what, eleven miles, and I got a puncture right outside that, um, the garden centre, and the guy there fixed it for free. Free. I tried to give him a tenner.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: That's nice.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: And he wouldn't take it, so I bought a plant instead and now I have a plant on my desk at home that I don't know how to look after.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Can we get back to the-

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah. Sorry. Fern. It's a fern. Done.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Okay. So.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: So the cost of the take-home, to be fair to it, is lower in hours but higher in people lost.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Is it though? We lose people on the phone screens too. Some don't show.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Some do, but not forty out of a hundred.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: I mean, big picture, we're trying to make the first step fairer and also not scare people off.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: That's both of them.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Right. It's, um, it's more like which kind of risk do you want?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: That's not wrong.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: One's risk is candidates walk. The other is we burn our own hours.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: And our hours are a thing we can actually plan for.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Whereas candidates walking, you only find out after.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Exactly, you find out after, so that's-

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Can I- sorry. Go on, Aisha.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: No, no, you go.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: It was just, um. The feedback. If we do the take-home we owe everyone an answer.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Yes. That's in the ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: But the video one, they get an answer from the call itself, don't they. Or soon after.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: They do, we usually say a few days.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: And they've actually met two people, so.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Yeah. The selling-the-company bit is better there, I'll give it that.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: I said that in the first meeting. Jonas said it.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: I did say it. I said it was too early to ask things of them.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: It was a good point. It's still a good point.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: What about scheduling, though? Two interviewers plus a candidate, that's the thing that always falls over.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Irina's been on at me about that. She wants a block each week.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: A recurring block would help. Tuesday afternoons maybe.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Tuesdays are bad for engineering. They've got the, uh, release thing.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Thursdays then. We can sort that out later.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Later being a different conversation.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Different conversation, yes.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Is that something Irina owns, or us?

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Us, I'd say. With her help.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: I do still worry it's a lot of hours. I'm not changing my mind on that.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Nobody's asking you to.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Good. Just so it's written down somewhere.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: It'll be in the notes.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: It will be. Um. Okay. Let me, let me just think for a second.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Take your time.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: I've got eight minutes.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: I was going to say the same.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Eight minutes is plenty if nobody starts on ferns.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Nobody will.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Right. Okay. The video screen, the forty-five minute one with two of us scoring on the shared rubric. That's the one for first-round engineering. The phone screen goes, and no take-home.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Okay. Good, I can work with that.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Fine by me. For the record, hours.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Noted, noted.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Good. That's, you know, done at least.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: I'll tidy the sheet so the video column is the main one.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay, I have to run, I've got the call.

utterances.speaker: Bashir
utterances.text: Go. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: Jonas
utterances.text: Diego, the form.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Yes. Going. Now.
